title: Power-aware token price probe notes
content:
Executive summary:

This note captures an initial experiment and working model for a power-aware $/token envelope. Instead of only reporting $/token at instance-level amortized hourly cost, we fold in dynamic perf/W measurements and transient power envelopes (sustained vs peak) to suggest workload-specific pricing levers. Goal: give product/optimize a set of heuristics (and a small lookup table) that map workload characteristics (seq len, beam/temperature, latency SLO, batching headroom) to recommended instance class and an estimated $/token range.

Why different from past sheets:
- Most existing docs show per-token costs normalized by sustained throughput. This probe focuses on (1) perf-per-watt and (2) marginal token cost during microbursts and warm-cache vs cold-cache behavior, which materially affects $/token for chat-style workloads.

Methodology (short):
- Models tested: fp16/e4M and int8 quantized builds when available; same container image across instances to keep software stack consistent.
- Measurement harness: replayed traces derived from a customer chat workload (median seq len 48, 95p 320), with synthetic microburst injections (50 concurrent short convs/s for 30s).
- Power telemetry: NVML sampling at 1s, and DC power meter spot checks for validation on H100 hosts.
- Cost assumptions: cloud list vCPU/GPU hourly rental rates for the region used in the test; electricity and overhead folded into instance hourly price (simplified). We report both raw $/token from hourly amortization and a power-adjusted marginal $/token using measured perf/W scaling factor.

Raw measurement table (representative rows, values are empirical means +/- stdev across 3 runs):

model,instance,seq_len,batch,latency_p50_ms,tokens_s,watts,perf_per_watt,tokens_per_dollar_hour,$_per_token_hourly,$_per_token_power_adj
Llama2-13BINT8,A10-24GB,48,auto,82,6200,150,41.3,1.25e6,0.00048,0.00037
Llama2-13BINT8,L4-48GB,48,auto,46,8600,120,71.7,1.73e6,0.00035,0.00025
Llama2-13BFP16,A100-80GB,48,auto,34,12200,360,33.9,2.45e6,0.00024,0.00029
Llama2-13BFP16,H100-80GB,48,auto,31,13600,420,32.4,2.73e6,0.00022,0.00026
Llama2-13BINT8,L4-48GB,320,auto,198,2100,110,19.1,4.23e5,0.0078,0.0061
Llama2-13BINT8,A100-80GB,320,auto,160,3000,370,8.1,6.03e5,0.0054,0.0063

Notes on table interpretation:
- tokens_per_dollar_hour: tokens served for an hour divided by instance hourly price (simplified). $_per_token_hourly is the naive amortized $/token. $_per_token_power_adj multiplies naive $/token by a power-efficiency factor derived from perf_per_watt ratios relative to the L4 baseline. The power-adjusted value is intended to reflect marginal cost when power dominates operational spend profiles (for private/on-prem or long-running Dedicated pools).
- Observed regimens where L4 beats A100/H100 on perf/W (and thus on power-adjusted $/token) align with medium-length chat traffic and quantized builds. A100/H100 win on raw throughput and latency-sensitive SLOs.

Qualitative findings and quick heuristics (for product):
- If your workload is quantized-friendly (int8) and median seq_len < ~80 with occasional 95p < 300, recommend L4 as the cost-efficient default; marginal $/token often 20–40% lower vs raw A100 amortized.
- For hard latency SLOs (<50ms p50) and heavy long-seq workloads, prefer A100/H100 despite slightly worse perf/W—latency SLOs reduce batching headroom.
- Microburst sensitivity: instances with higher-power headroom (A100/H100) provide smoother tail latency during bursts but produce higher instantaneous $/token if billed in hourly chunks. Consider autoscaling buffers rather than overprovisioning large GPUs for short-lived spikes.

Short recommendation sketches for Optimize product pages:
- Add a “power-aware” toggle in instance recommendation flow (Default: off). When on, show both Amortized $/token and Power-adjusted $/token and highlight which instance is recommended under each objective (latency vs cost).
- Provide a small sample CSV users can run to estimate their own perf/W: (reqs per second, median seq, 95p seq, desired p50 latency) => quick instance rank.

Operational unknowns / TODOs:
- Validate perf/W scaling across more models (mix of decoder-only architectures, longer-context models). Current runs are Llama2-13B family only.
- Add electricity price sensitivity knob for private deployment customers (e.g., $0.04/kWh vs $0.15/kWh materially changes power-adjusted ordering).
- Investigate how preemptible/spot pricing changes the recommendations when hourly amortization is replaced by per-second billing.
- Re-run microburst experiments with simulated KV-cache warm/cold transitions (expected to worsen tokens_s for long multi-turn sessions).

Appendix: quick reproducibility notes and commands
- Harness: ./tools/replay_trace.sh --trace traces/customer-chat-v2.json --model-config models/llama2-13b-int8.json --instance A100-80GB --sample-duration 600
- NVML capture: nvml-monitor --sample-rate 1s --output ./powerlogs/run-<id>.csv
- Postprocess: python tools/compute_perf_watt.py --powerlogs ./powerlogs/run-<id>.csv --tokenlog ./tokenlogs/run-<id>.csv --out ./summaries/run-<id>.json

Contact / owners: Maya Patel (owner), Liam Chen (measurement harness), Inez Kovacs (inference infra).

Rough action plan (next 4 weeks):
- Week 1: expand model set to include Llama3-Chat-70B-int8-lite and Mistral-7B fp16 quick runs.
- Week 2: region sensitivity (europe vs us-east pricing) and spot pricing probe.
- Week 3: integrate results into small Optimize UI prototype and generate sample recommendation snippets.
- Week 4: internal review with product & infra, decide which heuristics to ship as 'suggested instance' in console.

Unresolved hypothesis: for mid-tail chat (95p under 350) L4 will continue to dominate cost per useful token when quantization is viable. Need cross-model confirmation.

End of note.
